learningObjective: Delineate the responsibilities of an SPMD-style compiler versus a distributed runtime (e.g. NCCL / MPI stack).

canonicalClaims.claim: The compiler decides which collectives to insert, at which graph boundaries, and on which mesh axes; the runtime is responsible for executing each collective on the physical hardware, choosing algorithm (ring/tree/…), managing streams, and handling faults.
conditions: The compiler has enough static information (sharding annotations, mesh) to emit collectives.
The runtime provides a collective API with well-defined per-collective semantics.
nonImplications: Does not imply the compiler is unaware of costs; cost models can bias its decisions.
Does not imply the runtime is topology-agnostic; NCCL selects algorithms based on discovered topology.

canonicalClaims.claim: Choosing the internal algorithm (ring vs tree vs recursive halving), tuning message chunk sizes, and picking which NIC / NVLink lane to use are runtime concerns, invisible at the SPMD IR level.
conditions: The runtime enumerates topologies and internal algorithms.
nonImplications: Does not imply the runtime always chooses the optimal algorithm; heuristics may be suboptimal for a given payload.

misconceptions.claim: The SPMD compiler chooses the collective algorithm (ring vs tree) for each AllReduce and emits algorithm-specific IR nodes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In modern stacks (XLA/StableHLO, PyTorch Distributed) the IR-level collective is algorithm-agnostic; algorithm selection is a runtime decision by NCCL/MPI.

misconceptions.claim: The distributed runtime decides which sharding a tensor should have; the compiler merely emits placeholder ops that the runtime rewrites.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Sharding decisions are compile-time in SPMD systems; the runtime does not re-choose them per iteration.

misconceptions.claim: Fault tolerance across ranks is a compiler responsibility because the compiler owns the graph and can insert retry logic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fault tolerance (retries, dead-rank handling, checkpoint restore) is a runtime / framework concern; the compiler does not manage process lifecycle.

misconceptions.claim: Physical topology awareness (which GPUs are on the same NVSwitch domain) is required at the compiler level to emit correct collectives.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Topology mapping is handled at the runtime via mesh-to-device mapping; the compiler emits mesh-axis-referenced collectives.
